key_highlights: Iron ore prices in freefall; BHP under severe pressure, headline suggests existential risk to operations
Energy stocks lift ASX on rising oil prices; tanker-war geopolitics support crude
Australian housing price falls accelerate dramatically; RBA signals it will not cut to rescue property
Property developer suspends 60% of workforce, signalling deep construction-sector distress
Consumer stress intensifies: second jobs surge, Australians report feeling poorer
Junior mining active: Kaiser reloads Tassie gold, Larvotto strikes gold-antimony-tungsten in NSW, Aureka acquires Victorian mine for $8.9M
Stokes family retakes control of Seven Network (SVA.AX), raising governance questions
BYD declares Australia has passed EV tipping point, pressuring legacy auto and charging infrastructure
El Nino intensifying in Eastern Pacific, posing agricultural and commodity supply risks
US midterms and Trump threats add global macro uncertainty

sectors.trend: Severely negative. Iron ore collapse threatens BHP's core earnings; however, gold and critical-minerals juniors (Kaiser, Larvotto, Aureka, Kaoko, Vanadium Resources, Piche) show resilience and M&A activity
sectors.implications: BHP.AX and RIO.AX face margin compression; FMG.AX exposed. Gold miners (GOLD.AX, NVG.AX) and critical-minerals names offer relative strength. Junior M&A (Aureka $8.9M deal) signals consolidation in Victorian mining

sectors.trend: Positive. Oil prices rising on tanker-war geopolitics; energy stocks are the ASX's leading sector today
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, and oil-services names benefit. Tanker-war risk (headline 34) supports sustained crude premium but introduces supply-disruption volatility

sectors.trend: Cautious. RBA unlikely to cut rates to support property (headline 36), keeping yields elevated. Housing price acceleration in falls raises NPL concerns for mortgage books
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face rising credit-cost pressure from property. Higher-for-longer rates support NIM but cap growth. Consumer stress (second jobs) pressures personal-loan portfolios

sectors.trend: Deeply negative. Housing falls accelerate; a major developer suspends 60% of workforce. RBA explicitly rules out rescue
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) under pressure from rising yields and falling occupier confidence. Construction names (WTC.AX, MDS.AX) face order-book deterioration. Residential developers at risk of further distress

sectors.trend: Negative. Australians working second jobs, feeling poorer. EV adoption (BYD) shifting auto demand. Cigarette tax debate pressures tobacco
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WBC.AX consumer lending stressed. BHP.AX downstream demand soft. BYD's EV tipping point (headline 44) threatens legacy auto supply chains and supports charging-infrastructure plays

sectors.trend: Mixed. Stokes family retakes Seven (SVA.AX) control, raising governance overhang. BYD EV momentum and AI-worker shortages support tech/infrastructure themes
sectors.implications: SVA.AX short-term volatility on ownership change. AI and skilled-migration themes (headlines 61, 66) support long-term tech and infrastructure capex

Housing market deterioration with no RBA rescue in sight

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX exposure; rotate into gold and critical-minerals juniors

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Housing market freefall and property-sector contagion
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight residential REITs and construction; monitor bank NPL data for early credit deterioration

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Consumer credit stress and rising NPLs
risk_assessment.mitigation: Favour banks with stronger capital buffers (CBA.AX); avoid high-beta consumer lenders
Maintain AUD hedging on export-revenue exposure; diversify away from US-listed equities

risk_assessment.risk_factor: El Nino agricultural and commodity disruption
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor wheat, sugar, and cotton futures; consider agri-commodity hedges
Position for higher-for-longer; favour dividend-paying defensives over rate-sensitive growth

opportunities.rationale: Oil rising on tanker-war geopolitics; energy is ASX's leading sector with sustained crude premium

opportunities.recommendation: Rotate into gold and critical-minerals juniors
opportunities.rationale: Iron ore collapse hurts majors; gold (Kaiser, Larvotto) and critical minerals (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche) offer relative strength and M&A catalysts

opportunities.recommendation: Long-term positioning in EV infrastructure and charging
opportunities.rationale: BYD confirms Australia EV tipping point; structural demand shift supports charging-network and battery-recycling plays

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce or hedge BHP.AX and iron-ore exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore in freefall; headline suggests existential operational risk; earnings revisions likely
Accelerating house-price falls, 60% workforce suspension at a developer, and RBA ruling out rescue signal prolonged distress

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain defensive dividend allocation in banks and staples
defensive_moves.rationale: Higher-for-longer rates support NIM; CBA.AX and WES.AX offer yield and relative resilience amid consumer stress

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 likely under pressure from iron-ore weakness and property-sector contagion, partially offset by energy strength. Expect choppy, range-bound trading with sector rotation away from materials into energy and defensives. AUD/USD likely soft on commodity weakness.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural headwinds from housing correction, consumer deleveraging, and iron-ore demand softness cap upside. However, critical-minerals transition, EV adoption, and AI-driven capex offer medium-term growth pockets. RBA constrained; no rescue cut expected. 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive for selective sectors, bearish for broad index.
